newsitem.title: ITALY: Ethiopian soccer players seek asylum in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian soccer players seek asylum in Italy.

text.p: Sixteen members of Ethiopia's national soccer team who had gone missing in Rome resurfaced on Wednesday and asked for political asylum.
Lawyer Mario Lana confirmed the request to reporters at Rome police headquarters.

Lana, who accompanied the players to the police office where requests for permits of stay are reviewed, said it was not clear whether they would be able to play soccer in Italy if their request was granted.
Fifteen players from Ethiopia's squad as well as the coach disappeared during a stopover in Rome before they were due to fly to Casablanca for an African National Cup match against Morocco.
The squad arrived in Italy on Monday afternoon from Addis Ababa and had been scheduled to fly to Casablanca on Tuesday.
Early on Tuesday morning, the 16 left their hotel with their passports and their luggage, according to the hotel manager.
Seven members of the original group were still in Rome.
"We decided to ask for political asylum a long time ago but this was the first time we had an opportunity," one of the players, who gave his name as Yimam Mohammed, told reporters.
He added that the group had spent the night between Tuesday and Wednesday "on the streets" then went to a local office of the United Nations in Rome to seek advice.
"We asked for the name of a lawyer and they put us in touch with Lana," he said.
"We want to stay here...I'm not going back to Ethiopia because of the political problems," another player said.
Lana said the 16 would be free to travel in Italy while awaiting an Italian decision on the asylum request.
Italian media said they could be looking for contracts with second or third division teams.
"It's too early to say if we can play in Italy. Now we are tired, very tired," Mohammed said.
It was not the first time that soccer players from Ethiopia, a former Italian colony, had asked for political asylum during trips abroad.

In 1991, fifteen players in Egypt for the African Youth Soccer championship sought asylum. Six members of the Ethiopian soccer team asked to go to United States from Egypt in 1989 and in 1986 three players asked for political asylum in Swaziland.
